Basic Audio Spooky Tooth Review Thread starter Thread starter Andrew Lamprecht Start date Start date Dec 27, 2011 Andrew Lamprecht Minion of One Dec 27, 2011 #1 I freaking love the Spooky Tooth!! What an awesome pedal.... you should all try one... with the blend knob, the left side is like a fuzzrite and the right side sounds like a superfuzz. All the tones on it are extremely useable. The low end control and saturation, you can dial in a nice fuzz face, purple haze sound and with everything all the way up you get a big muff type sound out of it. You can do a bunch of the old 60s psychadelic stuff and everything. It's just so versatile and everything sounds good. Obviously the fuzz face setting I dialed in doesn't sound as good as the sunface I had but the big muff sounds better than the newer ones i have tried and it has so many of it's own tones going on...... I love this thing. It even gets really overdrive like with the saturation, low end almost all the way down. Cleans up almost as well as the sunface.... ahhhhH!!!!!!!!!!!! Very gritty almost break up type sounds...... My favorite setting is setting the gain about halfway, the low end all the way down, the blend about 3:00 (on the superfuzz side) and the volume almost all the way up. My favorite feature is the in between settings on the blend knob. This pedal is really close to the superfuzz with the knob all the way to the right and very fuzzrite (or at least ventures type music) all the way to the left... all the in between settings and super cool sounds I haven't heard before. LOVE THEM. This pedal has a really versatile range...... like I said, almost breakup to full on superfuzz where the amp feels like it is about to blow up. I really dig this pedal... I've always felt fuzz was just an add on or a cool effect to use every once in a while but with this pedal I could see someone using this pedal (with how versatile it is) all the time or even creating their own sound with it. Love it!! Thanks Basic Audio!!   MetalManiac Li'l Junior Member Dec 27, 2011 #2 Re: Basic Audio Spooky Tooth Review ICEMANNED AGAIN !!! It's a gray pedal with a lime green led.. :dot:   TwilightOdyssey Darkness on the edge of Tone Dec 27, 2011 #4 Re: Basic Audio Spooky Tooth Review This pedal has caught my eye since you posted about it before. I am very interested in this one. Can you tell me more about your associated gear -- guitar/amp/cab -- and what style of music you play? - **Archive parent:** Spooky Tooth
- **Builder:** Basic Audio
- **Catalog type:** Fuzz
- **Identity:** Medium/high-gain silicon fuzz drawing from late-1960s Orpheum and Manny's-style fuzz references, with stage-interaction Texture and Saturation controls. [1][2]

- **TEXTURE:** Changes the contribution/relationship of the gain stages.
- **SATURATION:** Controls low-frequency drive into the later stage.
- **FUZZ:** Overall fuzz level. [1][2]

- Basic Audio identifies the sound/design as drawing from **Orpheum** and **Manny's** late-1960s fuzz references.
- This is lineage/reference information, not a claim of exact historical schematic identity. [1]

- **Technology:** Silicon.
- Exact production transistor part number is not publicly documented.

- Exact clipping-device type and part number are not publicly documented.

- **9V center-negative** operation with battery support. [1]

- No numbered electronic revision established.
- Finish changes are cosmetic.

Basic Audio describes Spooky Tooth around sag, bloom, sustain and squish. Texture changes the stage relationship and Saturation changes how much low-end material drives the later section, allowing lighter fuzz to move toward thicker and more compressed textures. [1][2]

- **Identity:** High
- **Orpheum/Manny's references:** High as builder lineage
- **Silicon technology:** High
- **Texture/Saturation functions:** High
- **Exact transistor:** Unknown
- **Exact diode:** Unknown

Basic Audio's exact-model page was cross-checked with Effects Database. The sources support the silicon implementation, late-1960s reference family and control concept. Exact semiconductor information is not published. [1][2]

Spooky Tooth — Basic Audio Contact Store About Menu Basic Audio Contact Store About Pedal colors are subject to change. I am a one man shop, please be patient. I will get your order to you as soon as I can. ← Back to Store Spooky Tooth Spooky Tooth from $200.00 Medium to high gain fuzz a la Neil young in box. Nice over the top amp melting sag and bloom when cranked. Octave up like tone in the middle Texture settings. Lots of sustain and squish on tap. Gain and low end clean up with Saturation and Fuzz knobs. The Texture knob blends between one and two gain stages for light to heavy gain. Based on the Orpheum and Manny’s Fuzz pedals on the late 60s. Silicon transistors.
